method: Read-only code and fixed-source contract inspection; no production modules imported, no tests, Gradle, device commands or new source downloads executed by this implementation review.
parser: Only a complete positive-duration reset nested through actual acyclic parent IDs under clientTransactionExecuted may yield configuration_dispatch_supported; mere timestamp overlap or configChanged ancestry does not.
The entire ancestry uses the same thread track/utid/upid/tid/pid/main-thread identity, contiguous depths and depth-zero root; known process lifetime bounds apply to reset and ancestors.

Unique exact IME package/UID process instance is required, and main-thread tid=pid must match the process PID. Missing/ambiguous instances remain unknown; this is not Binder/service-process identity proof.
Missing parent, zero/incomplete durations, unknown or nonzero loss/error stats, missing readiness/end/bounds and invalid thread identity cannot create positive caller evidence.
BOOTTIME metadata and clock snapshots are required for raw elapsed-time comparisons; unknown mapping leaves window/offset unknown while preserving any otherwise valid trace-local ancestry.
Both raw windows must be fully covered for overall recorded analysis; individual observed facts remain available without promoting incomplete capture or original comparison.
No SettingsObserver inference is made from absent transaction ancestry, absent reset slices, final configuration snapshots, or old tracker counts.
CSV/JSON shapes, integer/finite-number limits, symlinks/nonregular files, row/query/file/resource limits and executing program/pinned-processor hashes are checked.
capture: The wrapper calls the existing keyboard comparison once without modifying original arm commands, show/registration budgets, 12-second raw windows or four region predicates. No wrapper command is inserted between original raw READY and show.

Configuration remains am/wm/view plus bounded process/task metadata, 120 seconds, 32 MiB file limit and two 4 MiB buffers. Input category removed to match declared scope; process stats poll is fixed at 1000ms.

Perfetto start ownership requires returned PID, recorded /proc start ticks and exact command-line digest. Stop rechecks comm/start time/cmdline in one finite shell before SIGINT; no global kill or root.
Settings restoration is attempted through the existing journal-guarded one-restore function before stopping capture. Summary-read exceptions do not bypass the independent stop/collection path.
A naturally ended, zombie or reused PID is never signalled. BEFORE_STOP remains unverified while preserving bounded trace originals; stop/exit/capture completeness are separate.
Oversize/empty traces preserve bounded file output and resource-limit failure, never recorded. Pull result, actual file bytes/digest and remote size are distinct.
Run-specific remote paths must be absent and not symlinks before creation. Ready/size paths must be regular and not symlinks; cleanup verifies both no entry and no dangling link.
Native trace duration limits residual capture when ownership cannot be proved. The shell recheck is explicitly not an atomic pidfd guarantee.
archive: Source repository/commit/run/attempt, test-only job and artifact association are verified separately; other executed modes are rejected.
Declared producer files match immutable Git blobs and verified checkout bytes; Python import origins and actual module bytes are checked before importing validators.
Capture report, original keyboard comparison/arm outcomes and analysis states stay independent. Missing/partial analysis is retained and never reclassified as complete.
Analysis validates the archived query bytes and their deterministic derivation with the source-bound parser; this review has not replayed an actual new device trace.
Source run/job failure cannot promote capture to recorded. Original payload bytes are scanned again after validation, then published exclusively with hashes and metadata.

Malformed or interrupted derived analysis bytes are retained separately as partial/invalid with validationError; original context/source validation remains mandatory, and reportedStatus is populated only after full deterministic validation.

An interrupted unverified wrapper may retain its older comparison summary; archive reports whether it matched the independently validated child summary. Completed/recorded mismatches are rejected and original bytes remain unchanged.
workflowAndDocs: New reset_trace/archive_reset_trace modes are separate from unchanged test/keyboard action paths; source checkout and archive branch are pinned to source commit/run/attempt.
A per-run finalize exists, but online restoration/stop correctness does not depend solely on the post-emulator workflow step.

Documentation states source-image and non-nested-loop assumptions, ten-second notification delay as a hypothesis, unverified original Notes24/8 and different five-second timing origin, and trace overhead as a new diagnostic intervention.
issuesResolvedDuringReview: Zero-duration reset could otherwise create supported classification.
Missing PID/TID or process-PID mismatch and missing depth-zero ancestor root needed explicit unknown handling.
FIFO opening and pre-validation path resolution needed bounded regular-file and symlink handling.
Early Perfetto exit previously discarded available trace evidence; it now preserves bounded originals without signalling or promotion.
Comparison summary failure previously could bypass stop handling; it is now isolated.
Remote dangling symlinks previously passed ! -e checks; ! -L is now also required.
limits: No new API37 trace exists within this review; runtime category support/readiness/data coverage remain to be observed.
Configuration-dispatch support remains conditional on the reviewed fixed framework implementation and no nested main-message-loop dispatch.
A trace without positive caller ancestry cannot establish SettingsObserver, and the ten-second mechanism is not yet the measured root cause.
No original Notes replay or acceptance repair, physical-device, real-model, Binder-identity, performance-budget or stable-fix claim is made.
Tests are run by implementation authors/root separately; this receipt does not claim independent test execution.
